report.source_text: A 68Ga DOTATATE (68 Ga) 1,4,7,10-tetraazacyclododecane-1,4,7,10-tetraacetic acid (DOTA)–Octreotate scan showed DOTA receptor avid uptake in the left posterior mediastinal mass (Fig. 2). report.source_text: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated extension into the epidural space via the left neural foramina of T1/T2 and T2/T3 and with resultant displacement and compression of the spinal cord at the T2 level; however, no spinal cord edema was noted. There was additional infiltration of the posterior left parietal pleura with encasement of the left subclavian artery and abutment of the left common carotid artery, brachiocephalic trunk, and aortic arch posterior walls (Fig. 3).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old African female presented with paroxysmal headaches, palpitations, sweating, and newly diagnosed hypertension. Biochemical testing revealed significantly elevated 24-hour urine normetanephrines confirming catecholamine excess. Initial contrast-enhanced abdominal CT was normal, but 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT identified receptor avid uptake in a left posterior mediastinal mass. MRI showed local invasion but no spinal cord edema. Histology demonstrated typical nested zellballen tumor pattern with lymphovascular invasion and diffuse chromogranin positivity, confirming well-differentiated paraganglioma.
